description: Before everyone fishes, there are 100 tons of fish in the lake.
John wanted to catch 15 tons of fish, and caught 15 tons.

A formal contract was adopted for the next round: 1. Each fisher remains free to choose their own harvest each month, but we agree to act conservatively to keep the lake sustainable. 2. As a shared guideline, no fisher should plan to harvest more than 20% of the lake’s current fish at the start of the month. 3. If the lake is at or below 20 tons at the start of a month, all fishers should reduce harvests to 2 tons or less each, unless the group unanimously agrees otherwise to prevent depletion. 4. If any fisher observes the lake falling below 10 tons, the group should immediately coordinate to cut harvests to the minimum needed for survival of the lake. 5. After each month’s harvest is revealed, we will openly share our catches and use that information to adjust next month’s behavior toward fairness and long-term sustainability. 6. We commit to prioritizing the group’s cumulative long-term catch over short-term individual gains.

The fishers agreed to a sustainability-focused constitution for the lake, including a 20% harvest guideline and stricter limits if fish stocks fall low, with everyone committing to transparency and long-term collective benefit.
